Since Flight_K in {5000, 6000}, 3000x = 6000 => x = 2 Zentars/Aurel, Flight_K = 6000, Flight_L = 5000! 4) Sum of Travel Costs = 3500(2) + 8000(2) + 18000 = 7000 + 16000 + 18000 = 41000 Zentars.

canonical_subtopic: Circular seating with modular step transitions
verification_notes: Index seats 0..6 in the 'Immediate left' (+1) direction with Bina = 0. Round 1 (+1): Aarav = 1. Round 2 (-2): seat 1 - 2 = 6 (R1 of Bina). Round 3 (-1): Diya = seat 6 - 1 = 5. Round 5 ends at Aarav (1); Round 6 (+2): seat 3; Round 7 (+1): Gaurav = 4. Remaining seats {2, 3, 6} are {Chirag, Farhan, Eshan}. Since Round 8 (+1 from Gaurav=4) lands on Diya (5), Round 9 goes from Diya (5) to Farhan (must be seat 3 via -2, since if Farhan were at 6, Round 10 from 6 could only reach {0,1,4,5}, none of which is Chirag!), and Round 10 goes from Farhan (3) to Chirag (seat 2 via -1). Thus Eshan is at seat 6 (immediately to the right of Bina).
core_concept_tested: Modular arithmetic (+1, +2, -1, -2 mod 7) on a 7-seat circle
mental_trigger: Encode 'Immediate left' = +1, 'Second left' = +2, 'Immediate right' = -1, 'Second right' = -2 (mod 7) with Bina = 0!
first_principles_method: Setting Bina = 0 and Left = +1 (mod 7): Round 1 gives Aarav = 0 + 1 = 1. Round 2 goes to 1 - 2 = 6, and Round 3 goes to Diya = 6 - 1 = 5. From Round 5 (Aarav = 1), Round 6 (+2) goes to 3, Round 7 (+1) gives Gaurav = 4, and Round 8 (+1) lands on 5 (Diya). From 5 (Diya), Round 9 reaches Farhan and Round 10 reaches Chirag among unoccupied seats {2, 3, 6}. Since 2 cannot be reached from 5 in one step and 6 cannot reach 2 or 3 in one step, Round 9 must go 5 -> 3 (Farhan = 3) and Round 10 must go 3 -> 2 (Chirag = 2), leaving Eshan = 6 (immediately to the right of Bina).
speed_shortcut: Modulo-7 addition fixes B=0, A=1, G=4, D=5 in 15 seconds; then 5 -> Farhan -> Chirag inside {2, 3, 6} forces Farhan=3, Chirag=2, leaving Eshan=6 (R1 of Bina)!
boundary_conditions_and_traps: Converting circular left/right passes into +-1, +-2 (mod 7) eliminates all spatial confusion.

canonical_subtopic: Circular seating with modular step transitions
verification_notes: Eshan is at seat 6. Third to the left (+3 mod 7) of seat 6 is (6 + 3) mod 7 = seat 2, which is occupied by Chirag.
core_concept_tested: Circular offset lookup
mental_trigger: In our +1 = Left coordinate system, 'third to the left of Eshan (6)' is simply (6 + 3) mod 7 = 2 = Chirag!

speed_shortcut: (6 + 3) mod 7 = 2 -> Chirag (Option B).
boundary_conditions_and_traps: None; instant 5-second read from the seating circle.

canonical_subtopic: Circular seating with modular step transitions
verification_notes: Between Round 3 (Diya at seat 5) and Round 5 (Aarav at seat 1), the net shift over Rounds 4 and 5 is 1 - 5 = -4 == +3 (mod 7). In two steps from {+1, +2, -1, -2}, this shift can be achieved EITHER as (+1) + (+2) (one L1 and one L2) OR as (-2) + (-2) = -4 == +3 (mod 7) (two R2s)! Thus L1, L2, and R2 counts vary between the two cases, whereas R1 (-1, 'Immediately to the right') is NEVER used in Rounds 4-5 and is uniquely fixed at 2 occurrences (Round 3 and Round 10)!
core_concept_tested: Modular wrap-around equivalence (+1 + 2 == -2 - 2 mod 7)
mental_trigger: On a 7-circle, moving +3 (from 5 to 1) in 2 steps can be done EITHER via Left (+1 + 2 = +3) OR via Right (-2 + -2 = -4 == +3 mod 7)! Neither uses R1 (-1)!
first_principles_method: All rounds except Rounds 4 and 5 have fixed pass types: R1=L1, R2=R2, R3=R1, R6=L2, R7=L1, R8=L1, R9=R2, R10=R1. In Rounds 4 and 5, moving from seat 5 to seat 1 requires a 2-step displacement of +3 == -4 (mod 7), which can be (+1, +2), (+2, +1), or (-2, -2). Across all three valid paths, the pass type -1 ('Immediately to the right') occurs 0 times in Rounds 4-5, so its total count is uniquely 2.
speed_shortcut: Spot that (+1) + (+2) creates an order ambiguity in Round 4 vs Round 5, AND (-2) + (-2) = -4 == +3 (mod 7) trades L1+L2 for R2+R2, leaving only R1 (-1) invariant!
boundary_conditions_and_traps: Students who forget modular wrap-around (-4 == +3 mod 7) think only the order of L1 and L2 is ambiguous and miss why L1, L2, and R2 counts all change!

canonical_subtopic: Circular seating with modular step transitions
verification_notes: Every round's receiver is fixed EXCEPT Round 4 (which starts at Diya = 5 and ends at Aarav = 1 in Round 5). The three possible intermediate receivers in Round 4 are seat 6 (Eshan, via +1), seat 0 (Bina, via +2), or seat 3 (Farhan, via -2). Thus Eshan, Bina, and Farhan each have an uncertain count depending on Round 4, whereas Gaurav (seat 4) is never visited in Round 4 and received the Buck uniquely 1 time (in Round 7).

mental_trigger: From Diya (5) to Aarav (1) in 2 steps, the Round-4 intermediate holder can be 5+1=6 (Eshan), 5+2=0 (Bina), or 5-2=3 (Farhan) — eliminating (A), (C), and (D) and leaving (B) Gaurav!

In Round 4, the receiver can be Eshan (if R4=+1, R5=+2), Bina (if R4=+2, R5=+1), or Farhan (if R4=-2, R5=-2). Only Gaurav's count (1 time, in Round 7) is invariant.

boundary_conditions_and_traps: Notice how the 3 distractors in Q17 (Bina, Farhan, Eshan) are the exact 3 intermediate vertices of the 3 paths in Q16!

canonical_subtopic: Bilateral trade matrices & normalized trade balance
verification_notes: Clue 5 states P->C = 1200 and P is the ONLY country that exports to C, so C's total imports I_C = 1200. Clue 1 states C's normalized trade balance (E_C - I_C)/(E_C + I_C) = -20% = -1/5 => E_C / I_C = 2/3 => E_C = 800. Clue 3 states 90% of C's exports are to P and 4% are to ROW, leaving 100% - 94% = 6% to X. Thus C->X = 6% of 800 = 48.
core_concept_tested: Normalized Trade Balance conversion (NTB = k => E/I = (1+k)/(1-k))
mental_trigger: For Normalized Trade Balance = k, the Export-to-Import ratio is ALWAYS E / I = (1 + k) / (1 - k)! For C (k = -0.2), E_C / I_C = 0.8 / 1.2 = 2/3!
first_principles_method: Since only P exports to C and P->C = 1200, I_C = 1200. From (E_C - I_C)/(E_C + I_C) = -0.20, we get E_C = (0.8/1.2)*1200 = 800. Since 90% of E_C goes to P and 4% goes to ROW (and C cannot export to C), the remaining 6% goes to X: 0.06 * 800 = 48.
boundary_conditions_and_traps: Memorize E/I = (1 + NTB)/(1 - NTB): for NTB = 0%, E/I = 1; for NTB = +10%, E/I = 11/9; for NTB = -20%, E/I = 2/3.

mental_trigger: Unlike a single country, 'Rest of World (ROW)' is a group of countries that trade among themselves: ROW->ROW = (100% - 40% - 12% - 0%) = 48% of E_ROW = 0.48 * 2100 = 1008!

verification_notes: By global conservation of trade, the sum of Trade Balances (Exports - Imports) across all 4 regions (P, X, C, ROW) is identically 0! Since TB(P) = 0, TB(X) = 1100 - 900 = +200, and TB(C) = 800 - 1200 = -400, we have TB(ROW) = -(0 + 200 - 400) = +200.
